title: なかなか～ない — “not easily ～ / just won't ～”
summary: なかなか with a negative verb means that something does not happen easily, or does not happen even though you expect or wish it to. It carries a feeling of difficulty, waiting or frustration.

patterns.form: なかなか ＋ 動詞ない形（〜ない）
patterns.gloss: なかなか来ない / なかなか解けない

patterns.form: なかなか ＋ 可能形の否定（〜られない・〜けない）
patterns.gloss: Often with potential negatives: なかなか寝られない

body.p: The adverb なかなか with an affirmative means “quite, better than expected” (なかなか上手だ); with a negative it means “not easily ～.” This entry is the negative pattern.
Use it when waiting does not bring what you want: バスがなかなか来ない, 問題がなかなか解けない. The verbs are usually ones that proceed naturally, or negative potentials, rather than deliberate actions.
Unlike 全然～ない, it leaves room for it to happen eventually; it just takes time. It is common when expectations are not met, as in 約束の時間になっても、友だちはなかなか来ない.

examples.ja: バスがなかなか来（こ）ない。
この問題（もんだい）はなかなか解（と）けない。
examples.tr: This problem just won't get solved easily.

examples.ja: 約束（やくそく）の時間（じかん）になっても、友（とも）だちはなかなか来（こ）ない。
examples.romaji: Yakusoku no jikan ni natte mo, tomodachi wa nakanaka konai.
examples.tr: Even when the promised time comes, my friend just won't show up.

pitfalls: Pair it with a negative. The affirmative なかなか上手だ means “better than expected,” a different meaning.
全然～ない means “not at all”; なかなか～ない means “not easily, it takes time.”
